title: Nothing in the cloud checks how fast the websites and the gym panel load on a phone
what: No automatic run measures page speed or layout jumps. The 10-minute outage alarm only asks whether each site answers. A hand run on 21 Nov found the gym-owner page jumping (0.265, over Google's poor line) and the member home page slow to show (3.0 s); no run would have caught either, and a slower change would ship unnoticed.
expected: A cloud run measures the main pages on a slow 4G phone after each change and warns when a page gets slower or jumps more than a set line.
who: gym owners and members opening the sites
fix_line: Add a cloud page-speed run on the main pages with warning lines for load time and layout jumps

title: No test ever runs a gym with hundreds of members, so slow big lists are never seen
what: The cross-role journeys make their own small fresh gyms, and the database tests only build a few hundred items to test size limits. No run fills a gym with 500 or more members and times the member list, Today, dues or the reports, so a page that crawls for a big gym would pass every check.
expected: One cloud run seeds a test gym with 500 to 2,000 members and a year of history and times the biggest panel pages and lists against a set line.
fix_line: Add a seeded big test gym and time its main pages in a cloud run

title: Phone app start time and the workout screen with a long history are never timed
what: The phone release test checks that screens work, not how long they take. The only run that reports slow starts is the real-phone robot crawl, which never blocks a release and stops green with nothing tested when its keys are missing. So an app that opens in 6 seconds, or a workout screen that lags for a member with years of history, would still be released.
expected: The phone test records the cold start time and the workout screen open time with a long history, and warns when either passes a set line.
fix_line: Time the cold start and a long-history workout screen in the phone test and warn on a set line

title: The watch test checks nothing is left running, but never measures battery use over a workout
what: The watch test on each watch change proves no wake lock is held after a rest and no busy loop runs in a quiet dimmed minute. It never measures how much battery or screen-on time a full workout costs, so a slow drain that is not a stuck lock would pass.
expected: The watch test also records battery use and screen-on time over a set length of workout and warns above a set line.
fix_line: Add a battery and screen-on reading over a timed workout to the watch test

title: The database check never looks for missing indexes, so 23 unindexed links passed and new ones will too
what: The database run checks broken functions at error level, security and feature tests. It never runs the speed advice, so the live database already has 23 links between tables with no index and 5 tables with no main key, and any new one added in a change passes without a word.
expected: The database run fails, or at least warns, when a change adds a table link without an index or a table without a main key.
fix_line: Add a check for unindexed table links and missing main keys to the database run
